Subject: Reserved tenor modulation & price-signal safeguard — sizing proposal for Inova

Tom / Inova procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our updated sizing workbook (INOVA_RI_ReservedSizing_v2.xlsx) reflecting the phased activation you described: a base reserved pool for steady-state inference plus a burst buffer for batch training spikes. Key asks from our side before I lock the commitment language:

- Confirm target 95th percentile qps for production LLM routes and expected monthly burst hours.
- Do you have a preference for a 24- vs 36-month reserved tenor? We flagged both options in the sheet.
- Inova asked about a cap on GPU cost pass-through risk if cloud/spot pricing moves dramatically — we proposed a "price-signal safeguard" (indexation with a banded cap). Would you be open to a shared cost model where increases beyond a predefined threshold are split?

I've included a short draft of the safeguard clause as redwood_price_signal_safeguard_draft.docx — it is deliberately simple (index reference + annual cap + one-time credit trigger). If you can confirm the burst profile and tenor preference, I can put this into the commercial term sheet for procurement review.

Next steps I propose: Inova confirms the numbers in tab "Operational Profile" and then we route the draft clause to Legal for a quick check. If you need, we can also do a 30-minute session with Marcus to validate expected utilization and pricing sensitivity.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — hoping to close sizing and get you to a pilot in Q1.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thanks for the materials. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Tenor: Procurement will push for a 24-month commitment with an option to extend a further 12 months; long tenors are a tougher sell internally given budget cycles.
2) GPU pass-through: we are not comfortable taking open-ended market exposure. Can you provide a concrete example of how the banded cap would work numerically (e.g., market index + 8% tolerance with a shared split above that)? Also we prefer a hard annual cap on passthrough to avoid surprise P&L impact.
3) Credits: If there is a market spike above the cap, procurement wants an escrowed credit or a one-time amortized credit to offset initial months.

I'll review the workbook with our infra team today and circle back with specific burst hours. If you can propose concrete numbers for the indexation band and the cap, that'll make it easier for procurement to sign off.

Tom Harris
CTO, Inova Health

Subject: Fwd: Reserved tenor modulation & price-signal safeguard — Inova asks (summary + ask)

Team — forwarding Tom's reply and my read of the ask. Short summary: procurement is pushing for 24 months (with an optional 12-month extension) and wants a hard cap on pass-through exposure plus an escrow/credit if market-driven increases exceed the cap. They asked for concrete numeric examples.

My suggested commercial approach (please advise):
- Tenor: offer 24-month firm + 12-month extension opt-in (customer pays for extension at prevailing discounted rate). This aligns with procurement cycles and lets us keep the longer revenue optionality.
- Price-signal safeguard: propose indexation to the GPU market index (we reference "RI-GPU-Index v1") with a band of +/- 8% annual movement. If the market index causes per-GPU unit cost to move up more than 8% year-over-year, we split the delta 50/50 up to a maximum of 12% annual pass-through to the customer. Above 12% requires executive approval.
- Credits: if the first-year realized pass-through push triggers >12% we offer a one-time amortized credit equal to 25% of the incremental cost to soften onboarding.

Operational asks for Marcus: can you validate the burst-hours assumptions in tab "Operational Profile" and confirm the expected utilization curve across month 1-12? If utilization skews higher we may need a larger base slab.

Kimberly — need quick P&L sketch on a 24m vs 36m case with the proposed 50/50 split and the 12% cap. If the economics are workable, I ask for approval to offer up to a 10-15% one-time credit (if needed) to get them across the line.

Laura — if Legal can draft a 2-paragraph clause that captures the indexation band, the split, and the exec-approval threshold that would accelerate procurement review.

I attached the sizing workbook and the draft safeguard doc we plan to send to them once we align.

Thanks — hoping to lock sizing next week.

Best,
Vanessa

All — quick decision: approve going to Inova with a constrained concession set. Details below for Vanessa to include in the commercial term sheet and legal draft.

1) Tenor: OK to offer 24-month firm with a 12-month opt-in extension.
2) Price-signal safeguard (approved structure):
   - Reference: RI-GPU-Index v1; annual band +/- 8%.
   - If index-driven per-GPU unit cost rises >8% YoY, cost delta is split 50/50 up to a cap of 12% pass-through to the customer per year.
   - If required pass-through exceeds 12% in any year, escalate to Exec for approval (Tom/further approvals).
3) One-time credit: approve up to a 15% onboarding credit (applied to first 3 invoice months) as an alternative to escrow. Kimberly, please model the P&L impact and confirm break-even thresholds.

Kimberly — confirm we can absorb the worst-case in Year 1 under the 50/50 split with a 15% credit. If the math doesn't work, come back with max allowable credit and we will adjust.

Marcus — please run the utilization sensitivity (base / +20% bursts / -20% quiet) and update the recommended base slab. I want the workbook turned around by EOD Tuesday so Vanessa can send the commercial term sheet by Wednesday.

Vanessa — once you have the revised workbook and the two-paragraph legal clause, send to Tom and procurement with a redlined term sheet and we will support any commercial pushback.

Thanks team — Sean
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
